source_text: τὸ λόγιον κατασημήνειεν ἂν, οἶμαι, τὸ τοῖς ἄνω συνῆφθαι τὰ κάτω, μεσιτεύοντος τοῦ Χριστοῦ. «Αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ἡ εἰρήνη ἡμῶν, ὁ ποιήσας τὰ ἀμφότερα ἒν,» κατὰ τὰς Γραφὰς, καὶ τῆς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων πληθύος τῷ συνδέσμῳ τῆς ἀγάπης ἀπαρτήσας τὰ ἀνθ
pass_a_gloss: …anō synēphthai ta katō… dēlōsis kai alētheia… Christos… pantote zōn entynchanein…
pass_b_english: Cyril: …the oracle would signify, I think, the below having been joined to the above, with Christ mediating. ‘For he himself is our peace, the one who has made both one,’ according to the Scriptures, and having fastened the human things to the multitude of the holy angels with the bond of love. And one must know that also blessed Ezekiel says the ruler of Tyre has put on every precious stone; and he counts these, which also all-divine Moses says have been set in the oracle of the judgments. And these were, sardius, topaz, emerald, carbuncle, sapphire, and jasper, ligure, agate, amethyst, chrysolite, beryl, onyx. And they had been arranged three each, and in whole four rows, the such placing sketching for us the firm in faith of those in heart and memory of Christ. For of faith is the three each, and as in Trinity a symbol; and of firmness the as in a square and equal-sided shape. For thus the oracle had been made, upon which also the twelve stones.

Cyril: And in addition to these at least he orders also something else to be woven-together with the twelve stones, saying: ‘And you will set upon the oracle of the judgment the disclosure and the truth, and it will be upon the chest of Aaron, when he enters into the Holy opposite Lord, and Aaron will bring in the judgments of the sons of Israel upon the chest opposite Lord through all.’ So then he names disclosure and truth, yet he has not still also made clear distinctly whether stones, or as on a small tablet a writing he has ordered to come to be. And I will remember a prophet saying, ‘Because for many days the sons of Israel will sit, there not being a king, nor a ruler, there not being a sacrifice, nor there being an altar, nor a priesthood, nor disclosures.’ But whether these also should be stones, or as on a golden tablet a writing of the names, the word will not investigate very much, and we will know they have been set unto a type, of Christ being present with saints. ‘For behold,’ he says, ‘I am with you all the days, and until completion of the age.’ And truth and disclosure is Christ. For in him we have known the Father, and he has disclosed for us his good will the perfect and well-pleasing, according to the Scriptures. For somewhere Christ said: ‘No longer do I say you slaves, you are my friends, because all things which I heard from my Father I announced to you.’ And truth also otherwise is Emmanuel, because he alone by nature is Son, and as from God God, alone holy, alone Lord; and by participation is the creation, and according to imitation, as many as he himself is thought to be. So then Christ is present with the saints as being thought in disclosure and truth, who also in person of the Father brings in the things according to us, always living unto the interceding for us. For this, I think, is the, And Aaron will bring in the judgments of the sons of Israel
